sections.overview: This long-armed octopus is known from the tropical Indo-West Pacific, including Indonesia.
sections.identification: It has long, narrow arms and distinctive white markings, including a teardrop-shaped ring and a U-shaped patch.
sections.habitat: The original description records it on soft bottoms in shallow water, at 0.5–7 m.
sections.diet: It probes burrows with its arm tips and traps fleeing prey with the web between its arms; the study did not identify prey taxa.
sections.behavior: The observed octopuses foraged by day in exposed sand, in view of potential fish predators.
sections.reproduction: The field paper observed adults and did not examine the species’ breeding cycle.
sections.ecology: Researchers documented postures resembling local flatfish, lionfish and sea snakes, but the defensive benefit was not experimentally tested.
sections.conservation: SeaLifeBase reports a global IUCN category of Least Concern for this species.
